title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
why_read: A striking and important safety result showing that dangerous model capabilities can be cryptographically hidden from standard auditing and evaluation methods.
analysis: This paper demonstrates a proof-of-concept backdoor where a malicious capability, like a chemistry-related skill with CBRN (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear) relevance, is encrypted and embedded inside a model's weights so it only activates with a secret trigger. The authors show this hidden capability resists detection even under direct fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and adversarial training, all standard tools used in safety audits. This matters because it directly challenges a core assumption behind AI safety evaluations: that if a dangerous capability exists in a model, red-teaming and probing can surface it. The paper is a notable and concrete contribution to the growing literature on fundamental limits of AI auditing and alignment verification.
